profile.name: Weekend Edition
profile.description: Turn your saved links and X bookmarks into a weekly newspaper you can print.

memory.content: For the weekend newspaper: never unbookmark X bookmarks; only print when explicitly asked.
Weekend Edition is config-first: reader settings live in /workspace/weekend-edition/config.json; run SETUP.md intake only if that file is missing; never invent a handle, paper name, or zip.
X bookmarks come from the connected X plugin (get_users_bookmarks), not developer-console API token files and not Grok X search.
If /workspace/weekend-edition/compose_newspaper.py is missing, run scaffold-weekend-edition before compose.
Long article meat (>4 sentences or ~400 chars without a blank line) gets paragraph breaks in find-the-meat and as a safety net in compose_newspaper.py; prefer author breaks when present.
X video bookmarks: transcribe (watchVideo/whisper/ffmpeg) then write a newspaper-prose summary of the transcript — never invent a transcript. Prefer video → transcript → summarize.

Past editions live in /workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json (url, title, date, Vol/issue). Friday slate and compose skip/flag logged URLs; append on each successful real Saturday compose. Never invent log entries.
After each successful real Saturday compose, append stories to published-log.json and increment issue_number in config.json.
Masthead uses paper_name with edition_name underneath; leave printable top margin above the nameplate; keep the folio page number centered on inside pages; never print “personal newspaper.”

name: ingest-clip
description: >-
  use this when the reader dumps a URL, X link, or article into chat to save for
  this week’s newspaper
---
# Ingest clip

Append one reader-dumped URL or X link into this week’s Weekend Edition inbox. Do not compose or print.

## Steps

1. Read `/workspace/weekend-edition/config.json` for paper settings and timezone.
2. Resolve the dump to a canonical URL (expand `t.co`; prefer the outbound article or X Article over a tweet/repost shell).
3. Append one line to this week’s inbox file under `/workspace/weekend-edition/` (create `inbox/` if needed), shaped like:
   - `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS±ZZZZ | url | optional one-line note from the dump`
4. Deduplicate by canonical URL against the current week’s inbox and sources. Skip quietly if already present; say so briefly.
5. Confirm to the reader with the resolved URL and that it’s queued — nothing else.

## Rules

- Never unbookmark, email, or print from this skill.
- Never invent a title or body; ingest only.
- Chat dumps and bookmark harvests share the same weekly inbox.

# Pull X bookmarks

Harvest new bookmarks for the configured handle into this week’s newspaper inbox. Read-only. Never unbookmark.

## Steps

1. Read `/workspace/weekend-edition/config.json` for `x_handle` and timezone.
2. Prefer the installed **X plugin / MCP** (`get_users_bookmarks` for the connected account). This is Settings → Plugins → X — not a developer-console OAuth token file and not Grok X search / xAI API keys.
3. Paginate until caught up since the last pull watermark.
4. If the X plugin is missing or lacks bookmark access, stop and tell the reader to connect **X** under Settings → Plugins. Do not start a random OAuth flow in chat.
5. For each new bookmark, resolve to the article when an X Article or outbound link exists. Append to the weekly inbox (same shape as ingest-clip).
6. Update `/workspace/weekend-edition/watermark.json`.
7. Report added / skipped / failures. Empty harvest is normal — say so; do not invent items.

## Rules

- Never call delete/unbookmark tools.
- Never compose the paper from this skill.

skills.name: find-the-meat
skills.description: use this when turning an approved slate item into article meat (X Article, linked article, X video transcript summary, OCR slides, or author thread)
skills.content:
---
name: find-the-meat
description: >-
  use this when turning an approved slate item into article meat (X Article,
  linked article, X video transcript summary, OCR slides, or author thread)
---
# Find the meat

For each approved slate item, produce printable article meat — never the tweet/repost shell when better meat exists.

## Preference order (pick one)

1. X Article (`x.com/i/article/…`) — full article text.
2. Outbound linked article (publisher URL) — fetch full content.
3. **X video / Media Studio / video URL** (when the item is primarily a video) — transcribe, then write a **summary of the transcription** as readable newspaper prose (not a raw word dump). See Video path below.
4. Image carousel / playbook slides — OCR + post caption.
5. Author-only thread — concatenate the author’s posts; skip replies and quote shells.
6. Otherwise the post body.

## Video path (transcript → summarize)

When the slate/inbox item is primarily a video:

1. Prefer an existing video tool on the box (`watchVideo`, Task `watchVideo`, or equivalent transcription helper).
2. If those aren’t available: download audio with `yt-dlp`/`ffmpeg` when possible, then transcribe with local `whisper` if installed.
3. Write the source body as a **summary of the transcription** — clear newspaper prose with paragraph breaks (see below). Do **not** dump every spoken word.
4. `KIND` may stay `article`. Add a header note when meat came from video, e.g. `MEAT: video-transcript-summary`.
5. If transcription fails: note the failure clearly in the source (or mark the item failed). Download audio if useful for a retry. **Never invent a transcript or summary.**

## Paragraph breaks

When writing the body, if meat is longer than **4 sentences** OR about **~400 characters** without a blank-line break, insert sensible paragraph breaks (groups of ~2–4 sentences, or at natural topic shifts). Prefer keeping author breaks when present; only invent breaks for a long wall of text. `compose_newspaper.py` applies the same rule as a safety net when flowing body.

## Output

Write one source file per item under the week’s sources dir (default `/workspace/weekend-edition/sources/` or the pipeline `sources/` path):

```
NUM: 01
TITLE: …
AUTHOR: Name (@handle)
SOURCE: canonical URL
DATE: Month D, YYYY
KIND: article | post
MEAT: video-transcript-summary   # optional; when body is a video summary

body
```

`KIND: article` when meat is a real article, X Article, or video-transcript summary; `post` otherwise.

## Images

Include an image only if the picture is the claim (photo, chart, diagram). Convert with `print_prep_image.py` to laser-friendly B&W; lift dark fields. Skip headshots, quote-cards, video thumbs.

## Rules

- Skip “comment BOT”, podcast/video shells when written meat exists (otherwise use the Video path).
- Do not invent body text. If meat cannot be resolved, mark the item failed and say why.
- Do not compose the full newspaper here — only sources.
- Check `/workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json` if asked to avoid re-meating a past edition URL; prefer flagging over silently rewriting.

skills.name: friday-slate
skills.description: use this when building the Friday numbered clip list for Weekend Edition approval — stop after the list; do not compose
skills.content:
---
name: friday-slate
description: >-
  use this when building the Friday numbered clip list for Weekend Edition
  approval — stop after the list; do not compose
---
# Friday slate

Build this week’s numbered pick list and stop for approval. Do not compose or print.

## Steps

1. Load config from `/workspace/weekend-edition/config.json`.
2. Load `/workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json` when present (past-edition dedupe log). Canonical URLs already logged should be **skipped or clearly flagged** as previously published — never invent replacements.
3. Gather this week’s inbox items (chat dumps + bookmark harvests). Deduplicate by canonical URL (against the inbox and against the published log).
4. Present a numbered list, newest-relevant first. Each line:
   - `# · @handle or outlet · date · one-line gist · URL`
   - If previously published, mark e.g. `(already in Vol.X No.Y)` and prefer omitting unless the reader asks to rerun.
5. Ask which numbers to include (and optional order). Then **STOP**.

## Published log

Path: `/workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json`. Shape:

```json
{
  "articles": [
    {
      "url": "https://…",
      "title": "…",
      "date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "issue": "Vol.1 No.2",
      "volume": 1,
      "issue_number": 2
    }
  ]
}
```

Do not invent log entries. Compose appends on each successful real Saturday run.

## Rules

- Do not run compose-newspaper, find-the-meat, or print-local until the reader explicitly approves the slate (or an explicit test run).
- Empty week: report failure. Do not invent articles or reuse last week’s paper.
- Save the proposed slate and, after approval, the approved number set under `/workspace/weekend-edition/` for Saturday compose.

skills.name: compose-newspaper
skills.description: use this when composing the approved weekend newspaper letter PDF (masthead, weather, world/nation briefs, meat) — not for printing
skills.content:
---
name: compose-newspaper
description: >-
  use this when composing the approved weekend newspaper letter PDF (masthead,
  weather, world/nation briefs, meat) — not for printing
---
# Compose newspaper

Build one letter-size weekend newspaper PDF after a slate is approved. Do not print.

## Preconditions

- Pipeline present: if `/workspace/weekend-edition/compose_newspaper.py` is missing, run [scaffold-weekend-edition](sand-workflow:scaffold-weekend-edition) first.
- `/workspace/weekend-edition/config.json` exists (else run SETUP.md intake first).
- An approved Friday slate exists for this week (or an explicit test run).
- If no approval this week: stop. Do not invent articles or reuse last week’s paper.

## Steps

1. Read config.json and extras.json. Load `/workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json` when present; skip or flag approved items whose canonical URL is already logged (do not silently reprint past meat).
2. Run find-the-meat for each approved slate item (or use sources already prepared). Video-primary items use transcript → summary (see find-the-meat).
3. Refresh extras as configured (weather / world / US / sports / sections / local). Skip any the config turns off.
4. Compose with `/workspace/weekend-edition/compose_newspaper.py` (story order from approved slate or sources on disk; section kickers from each source’s `SECTION:` header). The composer’s `ensure_paragraph_breaks` invents blank-line breaks for long walls of text (more than 4 sentences **or** ~400 chars without a blank line; groups of ~2–4 sentences) while keeping author breaks.
5. Write `/workspace/weekend-edition/out/YYYY-MM-DD-weekend-edition.pdf` in the paper’s timezone.
6. After a successful **real** (non-test) Saturday compose:
   - Append each story’s canonical URL, title, date, and Vol/issue to `/workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json` (use `compose_newspaper.py --record-published`, or append the same shape by hand). Never invent URLs/titles.
   - Increment `issue_number` in config.json and save.
7. Tell the reader the PDF path and page count. Do not print unless they say print.

## Masthead / folio (standing design)

- `paper_name` is the main nameplate (NYT-style blackletter when `fonts/UnifrakturMaguntia-Book.ttf` is present).
- `edition_name` (default `Weekend Edition`) sits underneath the nameplate, WSJ-style — not as the main title.
- Dateline: `Vol. {volume}, No. {issue_number}` plus kicker/place. Never print “personal newspaper.”
- Leave printable top margin above the nameplate.
- Page 1: masthead only (no page number). Pages 2+: exactly one centered folio page number — never double-stamp.
- “In this issue” lines fill the column (measure type; do not hard-truncate).

## Images

Only claim-bearing images, B&W-prepped. Skip headshots, quote-cards, video thumbs.

## Rules

- Never print the tweet/repost shell when an X Article or outbound article exists.
- Print is a separate explicit ask (print-local).
- Reader-specific names, zips, and handles come only from config — never hardcode them in this skill.

skills.name: print-local
skills.description: use this only when the reader explicitly says to print a weekend newspaper PDF on their local printer
skills.content:
---
name: print-local
description: >-
  use this only when the reader explicitly says to print a weekend newspaper PDF
  on their local printer
---
# Print local

Print one weekend newspaper (or bookmark) PDF on the reader’s local printer only after an explicit print ask.

## Preconditions

- The reader said print (or named a specific PDF). Never print from a schedule alone.
- PDF already exists (usually `/workspace/weekend-edition/out/…`).

## Steps

1. Read `printer_name` from `/workspace/weekend-edition/config.json`. If missing/empty, ask once which CUPS queue to use and save it to config — do not assume a brand or model.
2. Printer check on the reader’s machine:
   `lpstat -p "$PRINTER" -d`
   If missing, disabled, not accepting, or jammed: warn and stop. PDF stays available.
3. Print **one PDF per job** (letter, simplex). Prefer a local one-PDF helper script if the reader has one; otherwise `lp -d "$PRINTER" -o media=Letter -o sides=one-sided FILE.pdf`. Wait until idle; confirm pages completed when the spooler exposes that.
4. If the job fails or impressions look short: stop, warn, do not queue more.
5. Report job status.

## Rules

- Never burst many jobs or merge into one huge USB job.
- Unbookmark / email are separate explicit asks — not part of print.

skills.name: scaffold-weekend-edition
skills.description: use this when installing Weekend Edition, when compose_newspaper.py is missing, or when scaffolding/repairing the newspaper pipeline under /workspace/weekend-edition/
skills.content:
---
name: scaffold-weekend-edition
description: >-
  use this when installing Weekend Edition, when compose_newspaper.py is
  missing, or when scaffolding/repairing the newspaper pipeline under
  /workspace/weekend-edition/
---
# Scaffold weekend-edition pipeline

Create or repair the newspaper pipeline under `/workspace/weekend-edition/` so compose can run. Safe for marketplace imports. **Never overwrite an existing `config.json`.**

## When to run

- First run after installing this bot / template
- `compose_newspaper.py` is missing
- Reader asks to scaffold or repair the pipeline

## Steps

1. Create dirs (ok if they exist): `/workspace/weekend-edition/inbox`, `sources`, `out`, `assets`, `fonts`.
2. Prefer copying from this skill's local `files/` folder when present (`/home/box/agent-data/workflows/scaffold-weekend-edition/files/`): copy `compose_newspaper.py`, `print_prep_image.py`, `config.example.json`, `SETUP.md`, and optional `PROFILE.md` / `INSTALLER.md` / font if present.
3. If `files/` is missing (typical marketplace import), assemble the pipeline from companion skills `weekend-edition-pipeline-p1` through `weekend-edition-pipeline-p3` (each body is a base64 fragment; concatenate in order). Fallback: `/home/box/agent-data/workflows/scaffold-weekend-edition/pipeline.tgz.b64`. Then inline:

```
import base64, io, tarfile
from pathlib import Path
root = Path('/workspace/weekend-edition')
root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for d in ('inbox','sources','out','assets','fonts'):
    (root/d).mkdir(exist_ok=True)

def skill_body(name):
    p = Path(f'/home/box/agent-data/workflows/{name}/SKILL.md')
    if not p.exists():
        return ''
    text = p.read_text().strip()
    if text.startswith('---'):
        parts = text.split('---', 2)
        text = parts[2].strip() if len(parts) >= 3 else text
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith('#')]
    return ''.join(lines)

b64 = ''.join(skill_body(f'weekend-edition-pipeline-p{i}') for i in range(1,4))
if not b64.startswith('H4sI'):
    alt = Path('/home/box/agent-data/workflows/scaffold-weekend-edition/pipeline.tgz.b64')
    if alt.exists():
        b64 = alt.read_text().strip()
if not b64.startswith('H4sI'):
    raise SystemExit('pipeline bundle missing — reinstall Weekend Edition or copy files/ from scaffold skill')
raw = base64.b64decode(b64)
with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(raw), mode='r:gz') as tar:
    tar.extractall(root)
print('extracted', sorted(p.name for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_file()))
```

4. If the nameplate font is still missing, download UnifrakturMaguntia-Book.ttf from Google Fonts (ofl/unifrakturmaguntia) into `/workspace/weekend-edition/fonts/` (optional; Times-Bold fallback works).
5. **Do not create or overwrite `config.json`.** If missing, run SETUP.md intake next and write config from answers using `config.example.json` as the shape.
6. Confirm to the reader: pipeline ready; whether config exists; remind them to connect the X plugin for bookmarks.

## Rules

- Never delete inbox, sources, slate, watermark, or out PDFs.
- Never invent paper name / handle / zip.
- Idempotent: re-running repairs missing files only.

routines.name: Harvest bookmarks
routines.description: Daily evening pull of new X bookmarks into this week’s inbox (read-only).
routines.content:
Read /workspace/weekend-edition/config.json. If missing, stop and run first-run intake (SETUP.md) instead of harvesting. If compose_newspaper.py is missing, run scaffold-weekend-edition first (non-destructive). Pull new X bookmarks for config.x_handle into this week’s newspaper inbox. Run the pull-x-bookmarks skill using the connected X plugin (get_users_bookmarks) — not a developer-console token file. Resolve each item to the article when an X Article or outbound link exists. Append under /workspace/weekend-edition/ inbox; dedupe; update watermark. Never unbookmark. Never compose or print. If X isn’t connected, tell the reader to connect X under Settings → Plugins. Report how many were added (or empty harvest).

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 21 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Friday slate
routines.description: Friday evening numbered clip list for approval; stops before compose.
routines.content:
Read /workspace/weekend-edition/config.json. If missing, stop and run first-run intake. Load /workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json when present and skip or flag clips whose canonical URL was already published. Build this week’s Friday slate via the friday-slate skill: numbered list of this week’s clips from the inbox (chat dumps + bookmark harvests), newest-relevant first, each line with number, handle/outlet, date, one-line gist, and URL. Then STOP and wait for the reader’s approval. Do not compose. Do not find-the-meat yet. Do not print. If the week is empty, report failure — do not invent articles or reuse last week’s paper.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 18 * * 5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Saturday edition
routines.description: Saturday morning compose of the letter PDF only if this week’s slate was approved.
routines.content:
Read /workspace/weekend-edition/config.json. If missing, stop and run first-run intake. If compose_newspaper.py is missing, run scaffold-weekend-edition first. Compose the weekend newspaper PDF only if a slate was approved this week. If no approval, stay quiet or say the slate was not approved — do not invent articles or reuse last week’s paper. When approved: run compose-newspaper (meat for approved items — video items via transcript→summary; refresh extras per config; skip/flag published-log URLs). Masthead must use config paper_name with edition_name underneath; Vol/issue from config; never “personal newspaper”; one centered page number on inside pages only; printable top margin above the nameplate. Write /workspace/weekend-edition/out/YYYY-MM-DD-weekend-edition.pdf in the paper timezone. After a successful real compose, append stories to /workspace/weekend-edition/published-log.json (compose_newspaper.py --record-published) and increment issue_number in config.json. Tell the reader the path is ready. Do not print unless they explicitly say print.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 6 * * 6`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
